newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon welcomes U.N. vote on Qana shelling.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon welcomes U.N. vote on Qana shelling.

text.p: Lebanon on Sunday welcomed a U.N. General Assembly resolution calling on Israel to pay more than $1.7 million for damage resulting from its shelling of a U.N. base in south Lebanon last year in which about 100 civilians taking refuge were killed.
Foreign Minister Faris Bouez told reporters:
"What happened is an important victory not only for Lebanon but also for all those countries subject to pressures that undermine their presence and role in the United Nations.
"Through this decision, the General Assembly determined the criminal responsibility. It expressed Israel's responsibility and took a clear stance with regard to the massacre."

He said Lebanon would look into ways to demand further payment of direct damages during Israel's 17-day blitz called "Operation Grapes of Wrath" against Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon in which some 200 people were killed, mostly women and children.
The U.N. resolution, originally sponsored by Tanzania on behalf of the so-called Group of 77 developing countries -- now with 132 members -- and China, received 127 votes in favour.
The United States and Israel voted against the resolution dealing with the financing of the U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon. Russia cast the sole vote of abstention.

The paragraph in the draft dealing with the damages assessment against Israel was put to a separate vote and received 66 votes in favour, with the United States and Israel voting against and 59 abstentions.

"The vote restored to the General Assembly its right to tackle political, judicial and financial-related issues, all of which form the particularities of parliaments. And the General Assembly is the parliament of the United Nations," Bouez said.
A U.N. inquiry last year found that Israel's shelling was unlikely to have been the result of gross technical or procedural errors, although that could not be completely ruled out.
